h1: The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon — A New, Clean Hotel on the Bypass Road With Easy Parking
intro: If you're driving into Yasothon along the bypass road and want somewhere new, clean and easy to park at — without circling for a spot in town — The Model Garden Hotel fits the bill. It's a midrange 3-star hotel that opened in 2023 at 555 Liang Muang (bypass) Road in the Nai Mueang subdistrict. The draw is simple: new, clean rooms with cold air-con, a smart TV and free parking right out front, with a 24-hour front desk, from around ฿670/night. Real guest reviews agree the rooms are clean, housekeeping comes daily, the air-con is cold and the value is strong — ideal for self-drivers and anyone who just wants a clean place to sleep. Just know up front there's no breakfast, and it isn't in the heart of the sightseeing area.

body.html: The Model Garden Hotel is a midrange 3-star hotel that opened in 2023 on Liang Muang (bypass) Road, Highway 292, in the Nai Mueang subdistrict of Mueang Yasothon. Why people choose it is clear — it's a new hotel with clean rooms and easy parking out front, so there's no driving around looking for a space in the busy mall area in town. Rooms come in Standard and Twin layouts in simple, warm tones with the basics covered for an overnight stay, suiting solo travellers, couples and self-drivers passing through who want a clean room in the few-hundred-baht range.

What guests consistently praise is that the rooms are clean, the bathrooms are clean, housekeeping comes daily, the air-con is cold and there's a smart TV. Rooms have free drinking water, a water heater and Wi-Fi. The hotel has a lift, CCTV, a 24-hour front desk and free public parking out front — that last one is a real plus for self-drivers. Check-in and check-out are quick and fuss-free, which is exactly the point for anyone who wants a clean room to sleep in without paying for services they won't use.

"New, clean room, cold air-con, easy smart TV, and really convenient parking right out front. A few hundred baht but the quality is above the price — perfect for stopping overnight while driving through Yasothon."

The location is on the bypass side of the road — easy to drive in and out of central Yasothon, but not right next to the walking and sightseeing areas or the Ban Singha Tha old town, which are a short drive in. The surroundings are more of a through-route, with convenience stores and a handful of restaurants nearby. The real strength is for travellers arriving by car who use Yasothon as a rest stop or a waypoint onward to other Isan provinces — this bypass spot is far easier to get in and out of than a hotel downtown. The nearest airport is Roi Et (ROI), about 50 km away.

To be straight with you, based on real reviews: this place focuses on a clean room at a low price, so there's no breakfast, no pool and no gym. In the morning you'll need to head out to a local spot or drive into town for food. Some reviews mention noise — both from nearby construction and within the building while the hotel is still new — and one review mentions finding a gecko in the room, which is fairly normal for new hotels around Isan. Some room types are a street view with no window, so if natural light matters to you, check the room type before booking.

Bottom line: if you already know you want a new hotel, clean rooms, easy parking, in the few-hundred-baht range, The Model Garden Hotel is a sensible, reliable pick for Yasothon. Its 8.3 from 26 Trip.com reviews (cleanliness 8.5, service 8.5, location 8.4) reflects it well — clean rooms, good value, easy parking, with no add-on services by design. It suits self-drivers, people here on business in Yasothon, or anyone stopping overnight on an Isan trip on a budget.

A tip from following the reviews here: booking via the Agoda, Booking or Trip.com apps is often cheaper than walk-in, and it's worth comparing all three before you book. When you book, pick a room type with a window if you don't want a windowless room, and ask for a room away from the main road to cut noise at night. Since there's no breakfast, drive into town in the morning for a local breakfast, or hit the morning market in central Yasothon before heading on.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon

faq.q: Where is The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The Model Garden Hotel is at 555 Liang Muang (bypass) Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Yasothon, on Highway 292. It's about a 7–10 minute drive into central Yasothon, the mall area and the Ban Singha Tha old town. The bypass spot is easy to get in and out of, ideal for self-drivers. The nearest airport is Roi Et (ROI), about 50 km away.

faq.q: How much does The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿670/night for a Standard room. There are Standard rooms (street view, some with no window) and Twin Standard rooms with two single beds. During long weekends or festivals rates rise to around ฿850. Always compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon include breakfast?
faq.a: No — there's no breakfast and no on-site restaurant, because the hotel focuses on clean, affordable rooms and strips out the extras. You'll need to head out for a morning meal, either at a local spot or by driving into the morning market in central Yasothon.

faq.q: Who is The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon best for?
faq.a: It's best for self-drivers passing through Yasothon, or people here on business, who want a clean room with easy parking in the few-hundred-baht range. It suits solo travellers, couples and anyone stopping overnight on an Isan trip. If you want to be next to the sightseeing area or want breakfast included, a central city hotel is a better fit.

faq.q: Are the rooms clean and good value?
faq.a: Most reviews confirm the rooms are new and clean, housekeeping comes daily, the air-con is cold, and the value is strong. It scores 8.3 from 26 Trip.com reviews (cleanliness 8.5, service 8.5). Worth knowing: some room types have no window, there are no extra services, and there's occasional construction noise nearby.

faq.q: Is there parking at The Model Garden Hotel Yasothon for self-drivers?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has free public parking out front, a real plus for self-drivers. There's a lift, CCTV and a 24-hour front desk, making it handy for anyone breaking up an Isan road trip or arriving late.
